key_insight: Independent price-minimizing scheduling of EVs and heat pumps can synchronize demand enough to overload a low-voltage feeder more than uncoordinated charging, with heat pumps making this effect much worse.
engineering_relevance: Feeder operators need coordination or transformer-aware control for flexible residential loads, because price signals alone can shift rather than reduce peak stress on distribution assets.
method: Simulated a rural low-voltage feeder with 97 buses and a 250 kVA transformer.
Evaluated 160 runs across seven scenarios, four seasons, and 0–90% EV/heat-pump/PV penetration.
Compared decentralized cost minimization, fixed schedules, and a central transformer-capped schedule.
evidence_signal: Across the simulation set, 30% penetration of each device pushed the transformer to 253% of rated capacity under decentralized cost minimization, with up to 478% at 90% EV penetration and first undervoltage violations at the feeder end.
watch_item: Results are feeder- and tariff-dependent, and high PV penetration creates a midday reverse-power-flow floor that can limit what any demand-side strategy can achieve.
paper_title: Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
